concept.name: Anchored VWAP
concept.definition: Volume-weighted average price computed from a user-chosen anchor bar - a significant high or low, earnings release, gap, or other event - rather than the session open, extending the VWAP logic across days and timeframes.
concept.intuition: Markets reprice after events; anchoring VWAP to the event measures whether buyers or sellers have won all the volume traded since that moment.
concept.mechanics: Same formula as VWAP - sum(TP x V) / sum(V) - but accumulation starts at the chosen anchor bar and runs to the latest bar, on any timeframe. Used as dynamic support/resistance; converging AVWAPs from multiple anchors mark especially watched zones.
concept.formula: AVWAP = sum(TypicalPrice_i x Volume_i, from anchor to t) / sum(Volume_i, from anchor to t).
concept.failure_modes: Anchor choice is subjective - different anchors give different lines, inviting confirmation bias; like VWAP it lags increasingly as the anchored window lengthens.
concept.misconceptions: There is no objectively 'correct' anchor - the tool measures the post-event volume-weighted consensus, not a hidden fair value.
concept.example: StockCharts' TSLA example: the session VWAP from the open was skewed by the first 20 minutes, while an AVWAP anchored at the morning low better tracked midday trade.
